title: Infrastructure, cloud resource and endpoint inventory
status_rationale: No production infrastructure exists for Unbound and no hosting provider is selected. No inventory of Echelon corporate endpoints or cloud accounts was located.
target_answer: Echelon derives its infrastructure inventory automatically from infrastructure-as-code and cloud provider APIs, reconciles the two daily, and treats any resource present in the cloud but absent from code as an unauthorized-asset finding. Every resource carries owner, environment, data classification and, where it stores tenant data, the tenant or sponsor cell it serves. Workforce endpoints are enrolled in device management before receiving access; unmanaged devices cannot obtain workforce sessions.
current_practice: Unknown; no evidence located. No production environment exists.
intended_practice: Select hosting and device management; generate the inventory from code and provider APIs from the first environment.
customer_statement: Echelon has no production infrastructure yet. An automatically generated and reconciled infrastructure and endpoint inventory is planned from the first environment.
residual_risks: Resources created outside the provider APIs the reconciler reads (for example a personal SaaS account) are not detected.
open_questions: Which cloud and managed PostgreSQL provider will host Unbound (CNV-ARC-001 requires managed PostgreSQL; provider not selected)?

title: Software, dependency and AI component inventory
status_rationale: SEC-SUPPLY-001 (proposed) requires locked versions, provenance and SBOM; CNV-GOV-009 requires an SBOM license check. Praxis offers an inventory command for Echelon tools. No product SBOM exists because no product build exists.
target_answer: Every Echelon release produces a signed SBOM in SPDX or CycloneDX listing all components with versions, hashes, licenses and provenance, including Echelon's own frameworks (for example Strata, Limen, Forma, Folio) and their PolyForm Noncommercial or commercial license status. The SBOM is extended with an AI component inventory: models and versions, providers, prompts and tool definitions used by product agents. Unsupported runtimes and database majors are flagged automatically; only allowlisted, locked dependencies can enter a build.
current_practice: No product SBOM exists. Praxis (praxis@12bf9951) provides an `echelon inventory` command that distinguishes native Echelon tools, repository-installed lifecycle components and installed @echelon-foundry npm packages for a repository; this is a development-tool inventory, not a product SBOM.
intended_practice: Generate SBOMs at build using standard tooling, attach to releases, and fail builds on unapproved or unlicensed components.
provable: The Praxis inventory command and the proposed SEC-SUPPLY-001 rule text can be shown. No SBOM.
customer_statement: Echelon plans to publish a signed SBOM with every release, including its own frameworks and AI components. Today only a development-tool inventory exists in Echelon repositories.
residual_risks: SBOMs describe declared components; vendored or dynamically loaded code may be missed.
AI model behavior can change behind a stable model identifier at some providers.
open_questions: Will Echelon components used in Unbound be covered by an executed commercial license before launch (CNV-GOV-007, CNV-GOV-009)?

title: Data inventory, data flows and isolation map
status_rationale: Unbound requirements call for an isolation map per data class (UNB-RCN-PLT-001), a SharedStoreRegister (CNV-TEN-001) and isolation of secondary stores including embeddings and logs (UNB-TEN-009). None is built.
target_answer: Echelon maintains a machine-readable data inventory generated from the declared database schema and service contracts rather than maintained by hand: each data class has classification, legal basis, owner, isolation key (sponsor tenant or partner), retention rule and permitted cross-partner sharing. The inventory covers primary tables, event streams, caches, queues, search indexes, object storage, logs, telemetry, backups, non-production environments, prompts, embeddings and evaluation datasets. A release fails if a new store or column lacks an inventory entry (CNV-TEN-001 AC-2 and AC-3). Data flow diagrams are generated from the same source.
current_practice: No data inventory exists. Requirements specify it. Strata (strata@c6a384ec) compiles declared schema into an artifact that could serve as the relational source of truth, but no Unbound schema exists.
intended_practice: Implement the isolation map and SharedStoreRegister as schema-checked registers; generate flow diagrams.
customer_statement: Echelon plans a data inventory generated from its declared schema and service contracts, covering secondary stores and AI artifacts, with each data class mapped to its tenant isolation key. It does not exist yet.
residual_risks: Data copied by people (spreadsheets, email attachments, support tickets) is outside schema-derived inventories.

challenge.customer_intent: Be able to answer where our data is at any time, for breach scoping, privacy rights and examiner questions.
challenge.adverse_outcome: A breach or privacy request cannot be scoped because data copies are unknown.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Manually maintained data inventories and diagrams are typically incomplete and stale within months of creation.
challenge.legally_required: FTC Safeguards Rule 16 CFR 314.4(c)(2) and NYDFS 500.13 require covered entities to identify and manage data and systems; GDPR Article 30 records apply to EU processing. These bind customers, and in some cases Echelon if it is itself covered; they flow to vendors contractually.
challenge.contractually_required: Common in data protection addenda and bank questionnaires.
challenge.historical_convention: Spreadsheet data inventory plus annual review.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not eliminable, but staleness can be eliminated in scope: if every persistent store must be declared to deploy, the inventory cannot omit a store that the deployment created.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Release check fails on undeclared stores or columns (CNV-TEN-001).
challenge.continuous_evidence: Inventory regenerated on every release with commit hash.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Schema-derived inventory with a deploy gate, plus periodic discovery scans to catch data outside declared stores.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes; an assessor can compare the generated inventory with the deployed schema and cloud resource list.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely, provided a human-readable inventory and diagrams are also produced.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Data stored outside declared stores (manual exports, third-party SaaS) is invisible to the gate.
supporting_arguments: Generated inventories cannot drift from deployed schema.
opposing_arguments: Unstructured copies made by people are the usual breach-scoping problem and are not covered.

title: Third-party service and external attack-surface inventory
status_rationale: No production service and no subservice organizations are selected. SOC2-013 requires a critical service inventory. No inventory of corporate SaaS tools was located.
target_answer: Echelon maintains a service inventory listing each third-party and subservice organization, the data classes it receives, the tenants affected, criticality, contract and assurance status, and a fallback. New SaaS tools, including AI assistants, require approval before receiving company or customer data. An external attack-surface inventory of domains, certificates and endpoints is generated from DNS and deployment configuration and monitored for unexpected exposure.
intended_practice: Create the service inventory alongside vendor risk management; automate attack-surface inventory from deployment configuration.
customer_statement: Echelon has not yet selected production service providers. A service inventory and an external attack-surface inventory are planned.
residual_risks: Staff adoption of free AI tools can bypass procurement.

title: Secure configuration baselines and drift detection, including database privileges
status_rationale: Strata exists as a pilot declarative PostgreSQL schema tool that compares tables, grants and row-level security policies for drift and discloses what it could not compare. CNV-ARC-004 selects Strata for declarative schema governance. Strata is not operated against any Unbound database; host and cloud baselines are not defined.
target_answer: All infrastructure, container, cloud service and database configuration is declared in version control and deployed only through reviewed pipelines. Baselines derive from CIS Benchmarks where applicable, with documented deviations. Drift is detected continuously and either reverted automatically or raised as an incident. For PostgreSQL, Strata compiles declared schema, grants and row-level security policies into an artifact, diffs it against the live database before every deployment, and reports items it could not compare as not-compared or unverifiable rather than as matches, so an unverifiable configuration is never reported as compliant.
current_practice: Strata (strata@c6a384ec) is a pilot tool tested against PostgreSQL 16: it creates and compares grants and RLS policies per its README coverage table and refuses deployment across PostgreSQL major versions. It has not been run against an Unbound database or a large migration history. No host or cloud baselines exist.
intended_practice: Adopt Strata for schema, grant and policy baselines; adopt infrastructure-as-code with CIS-derived baselines; run drift detection continuously.
provable: Strata's source, tests and coverage table at commit c6a384ec can be shown as a tool capability. Nothing shows a configured Echelon production baseline.
customer_statement: Echelon's own Strata tool can declare PostgreSQL schema, grants and row-level security policies and detect drift, disclosing anything it could not verify. It has not yet been used on a production Unbound database. Host and cloud configuration baselines are planned.
residual_risks: Strata supports only PostgreSQL 16 and is pilot status; managed-provider defaults outside the declared schema (for example provider-created roles) may not be modeled.
Configuration items not modeled by any tool remain manual.

challenge.customer_intent: Be confident that systems are hardened and stay hardened.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Misconfigured storage, excessive database grants or disabled row-level security expose data.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Periodic manual configuration reviews and scanner snapshots catch drift late and miss items the scanner does not model while reporting them as passing.
challenge.legally_required: Not specifically required by statute for a vendor; PCI DSS requires configuration standards for in-scope systems, which Unbound is not expected to have.
challenge.contractually_required: Common questionnaire item; rarely a contract term.
challenge.historical_convention: Hardening checklists, annual review, configuration scans.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Manual production changes can be eliminated by removing interactive administrative paths (CNV-PLT-010 makes database admin roles break-glass only).
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Declarative deployment with pre-deploy diff and fail-closed handling of not-compared items.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Each deployment yields a diff report with explicit matches, differs, not-compared and unverifiable states.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Declarative configuration with honest coverage disclosure, as Strata implements for PostgreSQL.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes; the diff artifact and coverage table are inspectable.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Likely for the concept; customers will still ask for CIS benchmark scan output.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: If administrators retain interactive write access, or if the tool silently fails to compare an object class.
challenge.conventional_cost: Recurring review effort and scanner licenses.
challenge.alternative_cost: Engineering investment already being made in Strata; pilot maturity risk.
challenge.alternative_risks: A single tool defect could mask drift across all tenants; Strata's own history records five such defects found and fixed during development.
supporting_arguments: Six-state reporting prevents the common failure of treating not-checked as passing.
opposing_arguments: Strata is pilot status and has not been independently validated.

title: Asset ownership, classification and secure decommissioning
status_rationale: UNB-TEN-016 (refined by RR-UNB-TEN-016-r1) specifies cryptographic erasure under dual control and a destruction certificate on sponsor exit. No asset register or decommissioning procedure exists.
target_answer: Every inventoried asset has an owner, classification and lifecycle state. Decommissioning follows a recorded plan: credentials and certificates revoked, data destroyed by tenant-scoped key destruction under dual control or by media sanitization consistent with NIST SP 800-88 on provider-managed media (relying on provider attestations), and a destruction certificate issued that states what persists (for example immutable backups until expiry). Orphaned resources are found by daily reconciliation against provider billing and APIs.
current_practice: Unknown for assets. The tenant exit and cryptographic erasure requirement exists in Unbound requirements.
intended_practice: Implement owner and classification fields in the generated inventory; implement tenant key destruction and certificates.
customer_statement: Echelon plans owner and classification for every asset and verifiable destruction on decommissioning and tenant exit, including a destruction certificate stating what persists. None is operating today.
residual_risks: Physical media sanitization on managed cloud services relies on the provider's attestation.
